findings.title: Invalid ERB closing tag breaks embed view
findings.body: The template closes the `if @topic_view.posts.present?` block with `<%- end if %>`. ERB will emit Ruby code `end if` with no condition, which is a syntax error, so rendering app/views/embed/best.html.erb will fail. Use `<%- end %>` instead.

findings.title: Raw HTML cook method bypasses sanitization
findings.body: Post#cook returns the post's raw HTML unchanged when cook_method is Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. Imported embed/RSS posts are created with this cook method and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders post.cooked with `raw`, bypassing Discourse's sanitization. Any script, event handler, or dangerous URL in imported HTML can execute as stored XSS. Imported content must be sanitized or cooked through the safe pipeline.

findings.title: Unescaped embed URL is injected into stored HTML
findings.body:
TopicEmbed.import appends `
...#{url}...` to the post contents without HTML-escaping the URL. Because imported posts use raw HTML rendering, a URL containing quotes or angle brackets can inject arbitrary markup/JavaScript into the stored post. Escape the URL or build the anchor with a safe helper.

findings.title: RSS content is HTML-unescaped and then stored as raw HTML
findings.body: Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed calls CGI.unescapeHTML on feed item content and then imports it as raw HTML. This turns entity-escaped markup such as <script> into active HTML and stores it without sanitization, allowing stored XSS from an RSS/ATOM feed. Do not unescape feed content into raw HTML; sanitize or treat it as untrusted text.

findings.title: NoMethodError when an RSS item has no content
findings.body: poll_feed calls i.content.scrub, but RSS/ATOM items may not have a content element and simple-rss can return nil or omit the field. This raises NoMethodError and aborts the scheduled feed-polling job. Use a safe fallback such as i.content || i.description || '' and convert to string before scrubbing.

findings.title: Missing open-uri require for remote import
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import_remote uses open(url) but the file does not require 'open-uri'. If open-uri has not been loaded by another code path, open will not understand HTTP(S) URLs and remote import will fail. Add require 'open-uri' and preferably use a hardened HTTP client.

findings.title: import_remote fetches URL before validating scheme/host
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read before validating that url is an allowed http/https URL. TopicEmbed.import only rejects non-http(s) URLs after the fetch, so untrusted URLs can cause open-uri to read local files or internal services. Validate scheme/host and use a hardened HTTP client before fetching.

findings.title: Feed fetch has no timeout or size limit
findings.body: poll_feed fetches the feed with open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) and no open/read timeout or body-size limit. A slow or malicious feed can hang the Sidekiq worker or exhaust memory. Use an HTTP client with timeouts and a maximum response size.

findings.title: Missing embed URLs can trigger full feed polling synchronously
findings.body: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) whenever feed polling is enabled and an embed URL is missing. This lets many unknown embed URLs on the allowed host trigger full feed downloads/imports synchronously, causing significant load and possible abuse. Feed polling should stay scheduled/globally debounced.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
findings.body: The embed script accepts a postMessage event if discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1. This substring/prefix match can accept a different origin, for example https://forum.example.co matches https://forum.example.com/. Compare e.origin to the exact origin parsed from discourseUrl.

findings.title: postMessage target is the full referer and is interpolated into JavaScript
findings.body: The embed layout sends parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>'). postMessage targetOrigin should be an origin (scheme/host/port), not a full referer URL; path/query can make the browser reject the target. The referer header is also interpolated into JavaScript; use URI(request.referer).origin and JavaScript-escape it.

findings.title: Throttle key set with separate SETNX and EXPIRE
findings.body: TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? creates the Redis throttle key with setnx and then calls expire separately. If the process crashes between those calls, the key has no TTL and the URL is throttled forever. Use an atomic SET ... EX 60 NX operation.

findings.title: content_sha1 updated even if post revision fails
findings.body: When an existing embed's content changes, TopicEmbed.import calls PostRevisor#revise! and then updates topic_embeds.content_sha1 without checking whether the revision saved successfully. If the post update fails, the embed record is marked as up to date and future imports will skip it, leaving the SHA and post content inconsistent.

findings.title: revise! returns true even when Post#save fails
findings.body: PostRevisor#update_post ignores the return value of @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]), yet revise! returns true if the raw text changed. Callers can therefore believe a post was updated when it was not persisted. Check the save result and surface errors.

findings.title: PostCreator side effects are not rolled back if TopicEmbed creation fails
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator#create and TopicEmbed.create! in a Topic.transaction. PostCreator performs non-transactional side effects such as enqueuing jobs before TopicEmbed.create! runs; if TopicEmbed.create! fails, for example due to a uniqueness race on embed_url, the transaction may roll back the post while the enqueued jobs remain. Create/verify the embed record before triggering post-creation side effects or handle the race explicitly.

findings.title: Migration uses create_table force: true, which drops existing data
findings.body: The changed migration now creates top_topics with force: true. In Rails this drops the table if it exists before recreating it. If the table already exists in any environment, existing top_topics data can be destroyed. Use a guarded create_table or a separate migration.

findings.title: New gems are not added to the Rails 3 lockfile
findings.body: The Gemfile adds ruby-readability and simple-rss, but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated. When RAILS3 mode is used, Bundler uses the default Gemfile.lock; if that lockfile lacks the new gems, installation/booting will fail. Update all supported lockfiles or remove Rails 3 dual-boot support.

findings.title: Non-standard X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL header
findings.body: EmbedController sets response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'ALLOWALL'. ALLOWALL is not a standard X-Frame-Options value and is ignored by some browsers, so it does not reliably restrict framing. If only the configured embeddable host should frame the page, use CSP frame-ancestors with that origin.
